s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with shortness of breath and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: Chest pain and shortness of breath for 12 to 24 hours
Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery
key_facts: 39-year-old Hispanic man
Presented with chest pain and shortness of breath
Symptoms duration: 12 to 24 hours
Past medical history of acute myocardial infarction 9 years ago
Vital signs: blood pressure 127/86 mm Hg, heart rate 56 beats/min, respiratory rate 17 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 97% on room air
High-sensitivity troponin T: 888 ng/L
Normal biventricular size and systolic function on echocardiogram
No regional wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram
No pericardial effusion on echocardiogram
Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiogram
TIMI flow grade 3 in the left anterior descending artery

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T and large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery

shortlist.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery and past medical history of acute myocardial infarction at a young age

shortlist.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T and large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery

shortlist.label: Coronary artery embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery and no apparent abnormalities on electrocardiogram

shortlist.why_kept: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin T and large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery

raw.rationale: The patient's high-sensitivity troponin T level is significantly elevated at 888 ng/L, which is a key indicator of myocardial infarction. Additionally, the patient has a past medical history of acute myocardial infarction and presents with chest pain and shortness of breath, consistent with another myocardial infarction event. The large filling defect in the proximal segment of the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiogram also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of a large filling defect in the coronary artery is more suggestive of a thrombotic event than a dissection.

rejected.label: Coronary artery thrombosis
rejected.why: This is a plausible cause of the patient's symptoms, but it is more of a mechanism leading to acute myocardial infarction rather than a distinct diagnosis.

rejected.label: Coronary artery embolism
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of an embolic event, such as a source of embolism or multiple vascular bed involvement.

rejected.label: Intracoronary thrombus
rejected.why: The presence of a large filling defect is consistent with an intracoronary thrombus, but this finding is more of a contributor to the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction rather than a separate diagnosis.
